nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$ and every real number $x$, the Farey staircase $A_n$ of order $n$ satisfies $A_n(x) \le \lfloor nx \rfloor / n \le A_n(x) + (\log n)/n$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Bounds comparing the Farey staircase with $\lfloor nx \rfloor / n$

nodes.summary: For every real number $x$, the Farey staircase $A_1$ of order $1$ satisfies $A_1(x) = \lfloor x \rfloor$.
nodes.title: The Farey staircase of order one is the floor function

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ be a natural number and $x$ a real number, write $A_m$ for the Farey staircase of order $m$, and let $D_n(x) = A_n(x) - A_{n-1}(x)$. Then $D_n(x) = \frac{1}{n} \left( \lfloor nx \rfloor / n - A_{n-1}(x) \right)$ and $D_n(x) = \frac{1}{n-1} \left( \lfloor nx \rfloor / n - A_n(x) \right)$.
nodes.title: Recursion between consecutive Farey staircases

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ be a natural number and $x$ a real number, and write $A_m$ for the Farey staircase of order $m$. Then $0 \le A_n(x) - A_{n-1}(x) \le \frac{\log n}{n(n-1)}$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Bounds on the increment of the Farey staircase

nodes.summary: For every real number $x$, the Farey staircase $A_0$ of order $0$ satisfies $A_0(x) = 0$.
nodes.title: The Farey staircase of order zero vanishes

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a real number $x$, the Farey staircase of order $n$ is $A_n(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^{n} \lfloor kx \rfloor / k$, the average of the first $n$ lower rational approximations $\lfloor kx \rfloor / k$ of $x$. For $n = 0$ the sum is empty and $A_0(x) = 0$.
nodes.title: Farey staircase

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$ and every real number $x$, the zoomed Farey staircase $B_n$ of order $n$ satisfies $B_n(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \lfloor (k/n) x \rfloor / k$.
nodes.title: The zoomed Farey staircase as a sum

nodes.summary: For every real number $x$, the zoomed Farey staircase $B_1$ of order $1$ satisfies $B_1(x) = \lfloor x \rfloor$.
nodes.title: The zoomed Farey staircase of order one is the floor function

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a real number $x$, the zoomed Farey staircase of order $n$ is $B_0(x) = 0$ for $n = 0$ and $B_n(x) = n A_n(x/n)$ for $n \ge 1$, where $A_n$ is the Farey staircase of order $n$. For $n \ge 1$ this equals $\sum_{k=1}^{n} \lfloor (k/n) x \rfloor / k$.
nodes.title: Zoomed Farey staircase

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n \ge 1$ and a real number $x$, let $f_n(x) = \lfloor nx \rfloor - n A_n(x)$, where $A_n$ is the Farey staircase of order $n$. Then for every real number $\varepsilon > 0$, only finitely many distinct real numbers that are at most $1 - \log 2 - \varepsilon$ occur as a value $f_n(x)$ with $n \ge 1$ and $x$ real; here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Finiteness of small floor gaps of the Farey staircase

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 1$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$ let $f_n(x) = \lfloor nx \rfloor - n A_n(x)$, where $A_n$ is the Farey staircase of order $n$; thus $f_n(x) = \lfloor nx \rfloor - \sum_{k=1}^n \lfloor kx \rfloor / k$. Every real number $y \ge 1 - \log 2$ lies in the closure of the set $S = \{f_n(x) : n \ge 1,\ x \in \mathbb{R}\}$, that is, $S$ is dense in $[1 - \log 2, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Floor gaps of Farey staircases are dense above $1 - \log 2$

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ have derivative $f'$ at the point $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the quotient $(\lambda^{-1} f(\lambda x) - f(x))/(\lambda - 1)$ tends to $x f' - f(x)$ as $\lambda \to 1$ with $\lambda \ne 1$; that is, the dilation derivative of $f$ at $x$ exists and equals $x f' - f(x)$.
nodes.title: Dilation derivative of a differentiable function

nodes.summary: Let $B_n$ be the zoomed Farey staircase of order $n$, let $x \ge 0$ be real, and let $p$ and $q$ be coprime positive integers. Then $B_n(x + pn/q) - B_n(pn/q) \to \frac{1}{q} \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor qx \rfloor} \log(qx/k)$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Limit of the Farey staircase zoomed at a rational point

nodes.summary: Let $B_n$ be the zoomed Farey staircase of order $n$. For every real $x \ge 0$, $B_n(x) \to \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor x \rfloor} \log(x/k)$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Limit of the Farey staircase zoomed at the origin

nodes.summary: Let $(a_n)$ and $(b_n)$ be sequences of natural numbers with $a_n \le b_n$ for every $n$ and $a_n \to \infty$. Then $\sum_{k=a_n}^{b_n} 1/k - \int_{a_n}^{b_n} dt/t \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Harmonic blocks versus the logarithmic integral

nodes.summary: Let $A_n$ be the Farey staircase of order $n$ and $D_n = A_n - A_{n-1}$. For every real $x \ge 0$, $n^2 D_n(x/n) \to \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor x \rfloor} (1 - \log(x/k))$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Limit of the rescaled Farey staircase increment

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.

breadcrumbs.label: Continued fractions and expansions of reals
